blocks.text: What the toolkits counted, on all three islands. Digital edition only.

These pages hold the survey data behind Chapter 02. Each toolkit has its own page, with the three islands in the same order as the rest of the book: Malé, Villimalé, Hulhumalé. Where a theme page prints a number, the same number can be worked out here.
We surveyed each island on two days, one weekday and one rest day, each in three blocks: 10:00 to 12:00, 16:00 to 18:00 and 20:00 to 22:00.

blocks.text: WHERE THE DATA IS KEPT

The groups' field sheets are kept in data/toolkit_survey_all_islands.xlsx, one sheet per island and toolkit (M-, V-, H-). The field sheets number some toolkits differently from the book: book Toolkit 3 is field sheet T5, Toolkit 5 is T3-A, and Toolkit 6 is T4. This appendix uses the book's numbers. Its pages are numbered A.01 to A.09, apart from the printed book.
Every street was walked in segments and each segment graded from A (active) to E (inactive), after Gehl's study of Perth (2009), from its doors, closed frontage, variety and detail.

cells: Graded D or E: 80% of the length

Graded D or E: 0% of the length

blocks.text: HOW THE NUMBERS ARE WORKED OUT

cells.text: Doors ÷ segment length × 100; for an island, all doors ÷ all length.
As recorded per segment; for an island, weighted by segment length.
Chapter 02 counts with each group's own FAR column. Worked out as floor area ÷ plot area, Malé's plots would give 33 dense rather than 31.
Out of 32 (the book's scale); the field sheet heads its total /36.
